shared_blocker: unpinned requirements and missing wheel, ABI, libc, VPS, startup, and provenance evidence

findings.evidence_source: Dockerfile FROM instruction and docker-compose.yml image instructions
findings.observation: The bot base reference is python:3.12-slim-bookworm with no digest and no platform flag. Compose also uses mutable postgres:16-alpine and ollama/ollama:latest references.
findings.consequence: The verified OCI index is a historical snapshot. Current tag resolution was not rechecked.
findings.required_next_evidence: A separately approved registry recheck, or an explicit digest pin.

findings.evidence_source: rehashed AMD64 and ARM64 config bytes
findings.observation: Both configs declare PYTHON_VERSION=3.12.15 and Cmd ["python3"]. Neither declares User, WorkingDir, Entrypoint, ExposedPorts, Volumes, or Labels.
findings.consequence: These are declarations in the base-image config. They do not measure the interpreter or describe the final bot image.
findings.required_next_evidence: Final-image metadata or an isolated runtime measurement.

findings.evidence_source: verified config bytes and local requirement files
findings.observation: No SOABI, ABI flag, or wheel tag is present in the preserved evidence.
findings.consequence: A Python 3.12 declaration does not select a wheel tag.
findings.required_next_evidence: Interpreter ABI measurement or an explicitly labelled assumption in a later stage.

findings.evidence_source: verified manifests and configs; layer bytes absent
findings.observation: Debian bookworm-slim appears only as a manifest annotation. No libc version or installed package revision was read.
findings.consequence: manylinux compatibility remains unknown for both architectures.

findings.evidence_source: requirements.txt and the absence of wheel records
findings.observation: numpy, pandas, psycopg2-binary, and uvicorn[standard] are declared without versions, wheel names, or platform tags.
findings.consequence: Neither linux/amd64 nor linux/arm64/v8 has demonstrated wheel compatibility.
findings.required_next_evidence: Approved per-platform wheel metadata, hashes, and provenance.

findings.evidence_source: requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, and Dockerfile RUN instructions
findings.observation: Production requirements are lower bounds. No lockfile, hash pin, or wheelhouse is referenced.
findings.consequence: The dependency install is not reproducible from the current files.
findings.required_next_evidence: An approved lock and artifact-hash design.

findings.evidence_source: rehashed OCI objects and local project files
findings.observation: Digest checks bind the preserved bytes. No image signature, attestation, or package provenance file was verified.
findings.consequence: Byte identity against earlier descriptors is not publisher authentication.

findings.evidence_source: approved intended-target record; no receiver inventory in this stage
findings.observation: linux/amd64 and linux/arm64/v8 are intended targets. No VPS provider, CPU, kernel, or container engine was verified.
findings.consequence: An intended architecture is not a verified production host.

findings.observation: The bot command is declared, and the bot service has no healthcheck. No container was started.
findings.consequence: Startup and health remain untested on both architectures.
findings.required_next_evidence: An approved isolated runtime test after image and dependency evidence exists.

findings.evidence_source: historical stage boundary and local source hashes
findings.observation: Historical live-order authorisation is BLOCKED. Current production authorisation was not read. Source hashes do not show that production is running those bytes.
findings.consequence: Source-level safety work remains separate from production runtime safety.
